about: The injected faults (design §44 §10.4, SDK1 Task 4). Read by `sdks/conformance/faults.mjs`, served by `fixture-server.mjs` when a request carries `loams-test-fault: <name>`.
notRecordings: Every other file in `sdks/fixtures` was captured from a real server, because a hand-written expectation only proves the SDK agrees with whoever wrote it. These cannot be: a retryable `unavailable` needs a dependency to be down, a mid-stream disconnect needs something to drop the connection, and `token_expired` needs a token endpoint that does not exist yet (MT, API1 Task 7). What is still real is the wire shape — status, headers, Connect error envelope, gRPC-Web trailer frame — because that is what the SDK under test has to parse, and it is pinned here so it cannot drift from the recordings.
howToAsk: Any request may carry `loams-test-fault: <name>`. `loams-test-fault-after: <n>` tells a `stream_drop` to stop after n frames. Nothing is injected without the header, so the same fixture server serves the plain corpus unchanged. An unknown name is a 400, never a pass-through.
verify: `node sdks/conformance/verify-corpus.mjs` fails if this file and the `FAULTS` table in `sdks/conformance/faults.mjs` disagree about any status, code, reason or required flag.

faults.name: unavailable
faults.about: A retryable refusal (R2): the dependency this read needs is down. An SDK retries this one — base 100 ms, doubling, capped at 2 s, three retries, full jitter — and stops after that rather than spinning.

faults.name: resource_exhausted
faults.about: The other retryable class, from backpressure. Distinct from `unavailable` because a caller usually wants to slow down rather than back off, which is why this is the one carrying `retry_after_ms` in its metadata.

faults.name: deadline_exceeded
faults.about: The caller's own deadline passed. Retryable, but only because the client chose a deadline it can extend; a server that answers this has not done anything wrong, and an SDK must not treat it as a server fault.

faults.name: retry_after
faults.about: R2's last sentence: a server-sent `RetryInfo.retry_delay` replaces the computed backoff, up to 30 s. **No proto carries `RetryInfo` yet**, so it is injected with the header a gRPC retry policy reads (`grpc-retry-pushback-ms`) and the one the API would use (`loams-retry-after-ms`). That makes this the fault whose shape is most likely to be wrong, and the one to re-check when `RetryInfo` lands.

faults.name: token_expired
faults.about: R1's trigger, and the reason it is in the registry: a rejected access token, as distinct from one that was never sent. An SDK refreshes **once** and retries once, then reports a second expiry rather than looping. No server can produce this today — `loams dev` has no authentication at all and its `WhoAmI` answers `not_implemented` — so without this fault R1 is untestable against anything.

faults.name: stream_drop
faults.about: The stream dies mid-flight: real frames from the corpus with real cursors, then the socket destroyed with no end frame and no `grpc-status: 0`. That is what a proxy timeout or a mobile handover looks like to a client. R7 says the client re-opens from the last cursor it applied and does not re-yield what it already yielded, and this is the only way to check it — a stream that ends cleanly proves nothing about resuming, and an SDK that only resumes after a clean end would pass here and be wrong in production.
